name: Li Hua and Tree
description: Li Hua has a tree of $$$n$$$ vertices and $$$n-1$$$ edges. The root of the tree is vertex $$$1$$$. Each vertex $$$i$$$ has importance $$$a_i$$$. Denote the size of a subtree as the number of vertices in it, and the importance as the sum of the importance of vertices in it. Denote the heavy son of a non-leaf vertex as the son with the largest subtree size . If multiple of them exist, the heavy son is the one with the minimum index. Li Hua wants to perform $$$m$$$ operations: "1 $$$x$$$" ($$$1\leq x \leq n$$$) — calculate the importance of the subtree whose root is $$$x$$$. "2 $$$x$$$" ($$$2\leq x \leq n$$$) — rotate the heavy son of $$$x$$$ up. Formally, denote $$$son_x$$$ as the heavy son of $$$x$$$, $$$fa_x$$$ as the father of $$$x$$$. He wants to remove the edge between $$$x$$$ and $$$fa_x$$$ and connect an edge between $$$son_x$$$ and $$$fa_x$$$. It is guaranteed that $$$x$$$ is not root, but not guaranteed that $$$x$$$ is not a leaf. If $$$x$$$ is a leaf, please ignore the operation. Suppose you were Li Hua, please solve this problem.
input_specification: The first line contains 2 integers $$$n,m$$$ ($$$2\le n\le 10^{5},1\le m\le 10^{5}$$$) — the number of vertices in the tree and the number of operations. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_{1},a_{2},\ldots ,a_{n}$$$ ($$$-10^{9}\le a_{i}\le 10^{9}$$$) — the importance of each vertex. Next $$$n-1$$$ lines contain the edges of the tree. The $$$i$$$-th line contains two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ ($$$1\le u_i,v_i\le n$$$, $$$u_i\ne v_i$$$) — the corresponding edge. The given edges form a tree. Next $$$m$$$ lines contain operations — one operation per line. The $$$j$$$-th operation contains two integers $$$t_{j},x_{j}$$$ ($$$t_{j}\in \{1,2\}$$$, $$$1 \leq x_{j} \leq n$$$, $$$x_{j}\neq 1$$$ if $$$t_j = 2$$$) — the $$$j$$$-th operation.
output_specification: For each query "1 $$$x$$$", output the answer in an independent line.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1797D — Li Hua and Tree [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
